`Benson Fireplace Sales OS — App Intelligence Register.md` (68 KB, FD root)

- Source path
- Knowledge (what it carries)
- App area (Start Visit / Customer File / Setup + Goal Lens / Quote Review / Proposal Prep / Follow-Up / Smart Context / Backstage/Admin / Training/Help)
- Implementation form (quick-fill chip / smart default / warning/blocker rule / checklist item / customer-safe explainer / internal-only note / source badge/fact / proposal category / follow-up phrase / do not use)

- Sensitivity (rep-only / customer-safe / manager-only)
- Priority (use now / use soon / later / triage / archive)

- **E** = 04 - Showroom (site maps, display photos, layout docs)

- **H** = 07 - Service/Install (Install Job Sheet, Service Order Sheet, Installation Letter, NFPA 211 section 6, Stoll QC issues, service photo set, existing customer-photo named files)

**Final Report** section at end with: rank-ordered findings, quick-fill chip candidates, blocker/warning rule candidates, customer-safe explainer candidates, internal-only guidance, outdated/duplicate areas, recommended next PR for Claude Code.

## H. The "more ideas than just the app" opportunities

You said: *"more ideas other than the app could show themselves."* From what I've read so far, these stand out:

1. **Voice-note pattern library** — extract objection patterns, proven phrasings, customer questions from the Apr 22 → May 7 transcripts. Could feed training, scripts, and the BSFA Smart Context. Not just app-feeding work.
2. **Past Jobs Reference library** (created TODAY, folder 08) — 15 customer/job folders with photo documentation. With minimal cleanup this becomes a portfolio/case-study resource for in-showroom conversations.
3. **Showroom Display Register expansion** — Drew has 50 first-floor displays catalogued. The cellar register is referenced but not yet in the GPT-ready bundle. Adding cellar = ~doubles the showroom intelligence.
4. **Training v2.1 four-part series** — currently flagged as canonical. Should be evaluated for whether it supersedes v1.0 (which is "current under management review"). Possible training package to publish for new reps.
5. **Email templates buildout** (folder 05) — 10 templates done. With minor extension to a few more scenarios (price-change notification, brand discontinuation, manufacturer rep escalation), this becomes a complete email pattern library.
6. **Knowledge transfer / successor documentation** — if Drew ever transitions out of this role, the structured library here is already most of what a successor needs. Could be formalized into a "Fireplace Department Operating Manual" deliverable for company use.
7. **Vendor relationship audit** — the Product Vendor Quick Reference identifies primary brands but doesn't capture vendor-rep contacts, account numbers (sanitized), brand portal logins, or relationship strength. Could become a Vendor Relations Playbook.
8. **Marketing intake → Past Jobs flow** — folder 08 currently has just one loose JPG + the new Past Jobs Reference. Marketing could become a stronger pipeline if integrated with the Past Jobs work.

## Bottom line

Drew, the audit found three things you didn't tell me explicitly:

1. **You already built most of the AI library** — what's needed is incremental extension, not greenfield design.
2. **September 2026 is a real production deadline** because Liam is exiting active sales. BSFA needs to be ready to take over his pipeline by then.
3. **Follow-up automation is your highest-value missing feature** — Liam's own 33% sales lift data + explicit product mandate. BSFA's current single-touch reminder logic needs to extend to a 4-email drip ladder by September.

The audit's "build from scratch" framing was wrong because it didn't read the docs you'd already written. The real work is **incremental extension and verification**, not greenfield design — AND it has a real deadline. Six BSFA P0 features defined in `strategic-context.md` as the September acceptance criteria.
